problems.note: The mechanical flag is valid: null is not an allowed se_basis code. Methods describe one average per participant per condition and a paired test, but the Results report t(364) for a study with 51 people. Methods also describe pairwise distances whereas Results describe centroid distances per participant. These inconsistencies prevent confirmation that the printed uncertainty counts each randomized person once. They do not establish an output- or pair-level analysis either. not_reported is inapplicable because a test and confidence interval are printed. No replacement can be confirmed, so printed is null. Clarification of the implemented analysis or an explicit unknown-basis code is needed. Preserve the printed statistics, do not derive participant counts from degrees of freedom, and do not certify this as participant-level precision.

summary: Read the complete 92,166-character markdown in consecutive chunks through the end of the references; the 17-page paper contains no appendix. Checked the seven requested estimates against their cited PDF pages using PyMuPDF text extraction, with table extraction also attempted. All non-null statistics and the six elaboration estimates’ participant counts match the correct outcomes, arms and contrasts in Tables 4-5 (PDF pp. 8-9). The individual semantic statistics match PDF p. 10; its analysis-specific participant counts cannot be confirmed and appropriately remain null. Other requested coding fields agree with the reported design and outcome definitions; participant unit and SD level for the individual semantic result reflect the paper’s description, not verified participant-level uncertainty. All seven mechanical flags remain valid unresolved coding problems: six null measure codes and one null se_basis code. No evidence-supported replacement was found under the current vocabulary. The semantic result’s contradictory degrees of freedom and narrative direction are source inconsistencies, not transcription errors. Comparing the paper’s outcome/contrast inventory with the current extraction revealed no missing eligible estimate under rules 4-6; order interactions and unreported cross-period after-AI comparisons do not supply additional eligible contrasts.
